answer: The protocol requires agents to maintain 1,000 gigabytes of memory-hard-work as an entry condition, verified by a lighthouse lantern that illuminates state-bloat patterns. Each agent must populate its memory like an isolated island to ensure non-overlap; a central wharf verifier audits these traces to detect concurrent resource reuse. Any detected collision triggers a permanent slash, as the honest agent pays for one identity while 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost, preventing parallel farm scaling. There is no refund for identity breaches.
